propositions: materialize_tickets creates a full fresh copy of the 620 MiB ticket tree (69,984 blobs) for every gate resolution with a content-addressed key that has zero reuse, producing 10^5x write amplification on single-file deltas

the tickets cache key (`tickets-<sha>`) advances every ~26 seconds with no reuse because it is pinned to the live tracker HEAD, so the same-key cache hit branch is effectively never taken despite the immutable-SHA caching contract in ADR 0005

concurrent gate resolutions compound the problem: N agents cycling gates produce single-digit GiB of fresh file writes per round, saturating disk I/O and causing CPU spikes and resource starvation on shared hosts

hardlinking shared paths between adjacent tree entries and materializing only changed paths via git checkout-index --force -z --stdin eliminates the amplification while preserving attestation integrity and ADR 0005 guarantees

byte accounting must distinguish entry_size (reporting, plain st_size), exclusive_size (st_nlink == 1, the increment for populate and evict), and distinct_bytes (per-inode ground truth), because apportioned st_size / st_nlink credits bytes never freed and breaks the eviction watermark loop

the .ticket-write.lock file is tracked and shared by hardlinks but has fcntl.flock semantics scoped to inodes, so sharing would invisibly deadlock entries; it must be forced into the rewrite set and never hardlinked
